summary: Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk studied under traditional teachers Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (~1959–1981). He founded Thrangu Monastery, served as abbot of Rumtek Monastery (~1968), and was director at the Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981).

A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied at Dzongsar Monastery (1950) and under Khenpo Dragyab Lodro. He held posts at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as head (1972–1985) and director (attested 1991) of Sakya College.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Khenpo Dazer studied under the traditional teacher Bötrül Dongak Tenpé Nyima. He served as a teacher at both Dzogchen Monastery and the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.
A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Thrangu Monastery (~1936–1958). He served as a teacher at Rumtek Monastery (1959) and became abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra in 1978.
Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.
Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Gochen Monastery and Riwoche Monastery. He served as chair of the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under several traditional teachers, including Shukseb Jetsun Chönyi Zangmo. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1960–1970), Kyoto University (1960–1970), and the University of Virginia, and founded Nyingmapa Wishfulfilling Center (1971).

A scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Rasvir Das, Dev Narayan Tripathi, Khenpo Shenga (~1920–1927), and Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (~1920–1959). He also taught at Men-Tsee-Khang.
Ki-yong Rhi was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions at Dongguk University, where his appointment is attested in 1983 and he was attested as professor emeritus in 2007.

A philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1908–1912), Kichinosuke Ito held posts at Hokkaido University (~1926–1934), the University of Tokyo as professor (~1934–1946), and Chuo University.
Working in Tibetology and religious studies, Kim Gutschow earned a PhD from Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Kim Knott held academic posts at the University of Leeds (~1977–2012) and Lancaster University (~2012).

Specializing in Indology and history/archaeology, she studied at Haverford College and Brown University under David Pingree. She held posts at MIT (~2004–2006), the American Oriental Society, and Union College, where she was a visiting assistant professor (~2007).

A religious studies scholar, she completed her dissertation at Harvard University (~1983–1992). She was an associate at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (1991) and served as assistant professor at Harvard University (~1994).

Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, he studied at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1984) and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya. He held appointments at the University of Tokyo, Eastern Institute, Toho Gakuin, and Keio University (attested 2015).

A linguist who attended Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu, he served at the University of Helsinki as Professor of Computer Linguistics (attested 1994) and as director of the BAULT research community (attested 2015).
Active in religious studies and Buddhist studies, Kin Cheung earned a PhD at Temple University under the doctoral supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).
Working in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, King Chung Lo completed a PhD at Leipzig University, supervised by Eli Franco in 2009.
A scholar in Indology and religious studies, King Pong Chiu earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under the doctoral supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).
